thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-gen (eu-west-1) p99 latency spike detected — threshold 1200ms breached (p99=1870ms, p95=540ms). Streaming tail rate increased. Alert routed to #incidents and on-call.
anna_oncall: Ack. Joining bridge. Any customer-facing errors? :phone:
lina_custsuccess: Seeing 3 active support tickets mentioning slow responses from our EU inference endpoint. Customers: 'SpinApps', 'EduSynth'. I’ll patch customers in a sec.
jay_sre: Quick checks: dash looks like sudden tail spike around 12:03 UTC. KV cache hit dropped ~30%. Prefixcache eviction count up. Links: https://dash.re/redwood/realtime-gen/eu p99 chart.
anna_oncall: Good call. mike, can you check infra-side (GPU queue, host/rt)?
mike_infra: On it. node queues show one host with long GC/oom-swap events around 12:02, but not full OOM. Rolling restart candidate.
jay_sre: Also seeing increased request fanout -> more cold starts for model shards. Streaming stall traces show few requests stuck waiting on kv-lookup.
anna_oncall: Runbook step 1: confirm whether this is prefix/KV cache eviction vs backend slow kernels. Step 2: short-term mitigation: enable fast-fallback route to quantized-v1 for realtime-gen-eu and scale up warm pool by +2. I'll trigger.
ops-bot: ACTION: routing policy update initiated by anna_oncall — adding fallback target realtime-gen-eu:quantized-v1, scale warm-pool +2.
anna_oncall: @jay_sre please watch p99 and prefixcache metrics during rollout. @lina_custsuccess keep customers informed.
jay_sre: Watching. p99 dropped from 1870 -> 990ms within 35s of route change, p95 stable. KV hits recovering slowly.
mike_infra: Restarted host r-eu-12 on nodepool-3 (graceful drain). After restart, kernel latencies normalized. No disk errors.
lina_custsuccess: Updated tickets: told SpinApps there's a mitigative fallback and we're monitoring. EduSynth flagged for follow-up.
anna_oncall: Good. Any indication this was config drift or recent deploy?
jay_sre: small deploy rolled 11:58 that adjusted cache TTL on prefixcache from 6m -> 1m for throughput test. TTL decrease may have caused higher eviction under burst.
anna_oncall: Noted. Revert TTL to 6m in canary-config on eu cluster. Keeps the quantized fallback active until metrics stable.
ops-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: prefixcache.ttl set to 6m in eu canary by anna_oncall.
jay_sre: After revert + warm-pool, p99 now ~430ms, p95 480ms (weird p95>p99 transient glitch but smoothing out).
mike_infra: Node r-eu-12 stable. No further queue backpressure.
lina_custsuccess: Customers acknowledge mitigation. They want post-incident summary when closed.
anna_oncall: Triage notes: root cause likely TTL regression from deploy + eviction + a single host kernel hiccup, causing cold-path fanout and KV misses -> streaming tail stalls. Mitigations: routing fallback to quantized model, warm-pool scale-up, host restart, revert TTL.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated — p99 back within SLO (currently 390ms). Monitoring for 30m. Incident channel will stay open for postmortem.
anna_oncall: Leaving a TODO for postmortem: timeline, deploy diff, test to prevent TTL regression, and automated canary guard on prefixcache TTL changes. Assigning to @jay_sre for triage doc and @mike_infra for infra checklist.
jay_sre: Will draft. Lina, include customer impact notes.
lina_custsuccess: Will add ticket IDs and customer quotes.
ops-bot: NOTE: incident acknowledged by on-call and marked mitigated. Close window starts at 12:34 UTC if stable. :white_check_mark:
anna_oncall: Thanks all. Stand down unless we see another flare. :thumbsup:
